note: Hand-curated league profiles. watch[] URLs are verified live before shipping; broadcast facts from league/rights-holder announcements — nothing invented.

mls.about: Major League Soccer is the top division of men's professional soccer in the United States and Canada. Founded in 1996 as part of the USA's 1994 World Cup bid commitments, it has grown into a 30-club league with purpose-built stadiums, designated-player stars and its own youth-to-first-team pipeline.
mls.watchNote: As of 2026, every MLS regular-season and playoff match streams worldwide with an Apple TV subscription — the separate MLS Season Pass ended after 2025.

uslc.about: The USL Championship is the second division of American men's professional soccer, with clubs coast to coast and a playoff format crowning a national champion each fall. It is the top level of the United Soccer League system.
uslc.watchNote: Full-season coverage streams on CBS Sports Golazo Network and ESPN's platforms, with select national games on CBS, CBS Sports Network and ESPN2.

usl1.about: USL League One is a Division III professional league built around emerging American soccer markets — smaller cities getting their first professional club. It sits below the USL Championship in the USL structure.
usl1.watchNote: Season coverage streams on CBS Sports Golazo Network and ESPN's platforms, with select games on CBS Sports Network.

mnp.about: MLS Next Pro is the professional development tier of the MLS pathway, launched in 2022. Most clubs are the second teams of MLS sides, alongside a growing group of independent clubs, bridging elite academy soccer and the first team.

nisa.about: The National Independent Soccer Association is an independent professional league outside the MLS and USL structures, built around club autonomy and open-league ideals.

nwsl.about: The National Women's Soccer League is the top division of women's professional soccer in the United States — the longest-running top-flight women's league in the country's history, drawing many of the world's best players.
nwsl.watchNote: 2026 games air across CBS/Paramount+, ESPN/ABC, Prime Video (Fridays), ION (Saturdays) and the free Victory+ app; every match not picked up nationally streams free on NWSL+.

uslw.about: The USL Super League (branded the Gainbridge Super League) is a Division I-sanctioned women's professional league that kicked off in 2024, running a fall-to-summer calendar aligned with the global women's game.
uslw.watchNote: Every regular-season and playoff match streams on Peacock under the league's NBCUniversal partnership.

usl2.about: USL League Two is the top pre-professional men's league — a summer proving ground where college players keep their eligibility while playing in front of pro scouts. Its alumni fill MLS and USL rosters every season.

uslwl.about: The USL W League is the pre-professional women's counterpart to League Two — a summer league connecting college stars, returning pros and top amateurs on the pathway to the professional game.

npsl.about: The National Premier Soccer League is one of the country's largest national amateur leagues, with community-owned and independent clubs competing in regional conferences toward a national championship every summer.

upsl.about: The United Premier Soccer League is the largest amateur league in the United States by club count, with promotion and relegation inside its regional conferences and national playoffs each season.
upsl.watchNote: Most UPSL matches are streamed by clubs and conferences; the league channel carries featured games and playoffs.

loc.about: The League for Clubs is a club-owned national amateur league founded on shared governance — member clubs hold the league itself, an alternative to franchise-style structures.

wpsl.about: The Women's Premier Soccer League is among the largest women's soccer leagues in the world, running summer seasons in regional conferences since 1998 — a longtime proving ground for players headed to the pro game.

uws.about: United Women's Soccer is a national pre-professional women's league playing a summer season in regional conferences, with a national championship crowning the season.

uws2.about: UWS League Two is the development division of United Women's Soccer — a first competitive rung for new clubs and young rosters on the way to the UWS national league.

apsl.about: The American Premier Soccer League is a regional amateur league with conferences concentrated in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic, playing a fall-to-spring calendar unusual among American amateur leagues.

swpl.about: The Southwest Premier League is a regional amateur league covering Southern California and the desert Southwest, part of the growing web of regional leagues feeding the national amateur game.

mpl.about: The Mountain Premier League is a regional amateur league serving the Rocky Mountain states — Colorado and its neighbors — connecting mountain-region clubs to the national amateur pyramid.

mwpl.about: The Midwest Premier League is a regional amateur league spanning the industrial Midwest, with a dense club map across Illinois, Michigan, Ohio and neighboring states.

cpl.about: The Cascadia Premier League is a regional amateur league for the Pacific Northwest, organizing men's competition across Washington and Oregon's deep local soccer culture.

cplw.about: The Cascadia Premier League's women's competition brings the same Pacific Northwest regional structure to the women's amateur game.

gcpl.about: The Gulf Coast Premier League is a regional amateur league along the Gulf of Mexico, with clubs from Texas through Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama and Florida.

ncaa1.about: NCAA Division I is the top level of men's college soccer — the sport's main development route in the United States for decades, feeding the MLS SuperDraft and the professional leagues every year.

ncaa2.about: NCAA Division II men's soccer balances scholarship athletics with smaller campuses — a competitive tier that regularly produces professional players.

ncaa3.about: NCAA Division III is the largest division of college soccer by school count — no athletic scholarships, but deep rosters and serious regional rivalries.

naia.about: The NAIA is college soccer outside the NCAA — smaller schools with their own national championship, and a long history of overlooked talent reaching the pro game.

ncaa1w.about: NCAA Division I women's soccer is the deepest college competition in the women's game worldwide — the backbone of USWNT and NWSL rosters since the 1990s.

ncaa2w.about: NCAA Division II women's soccer pairs scholarship athletics with smaller campuses across every region of the country.

mlsnext.about: MLS NEXT is the elite boys' academy platform run by Major League Soccer — the primary development competition for MLS academies and top independent clubs.

ecnlb.about: The ECNL Boys is a national elite youth platform run by the Elite Clubs National League, competing with MLS NEXT at the top of the boys' development landscape.

ecnlg.about: The ECNL Girls is the leading elite platform in girls' youth soccer, the primary college-recruiting showcase environment in the women's game.

ecrlb.about: The ECNL Regional League Boys is the second competitive tier of the ECNL boys' platform, connecting regional club competition to national ECNL events.

ecrlg.about: The ECNL Regional League Girls is the second competitive tier of the ECNL girls' platform, a step below the national ECNL Girls league.

ga.about: The Girls Academy is a club-governed national platform in elite girls' youth soccer, formed in 2020 with player development and college placement at its center.

gaa.about: GA Aspire is the Girls Academy's development tier, a competitive entry point for clubs building toward full Girls Academy membership.

ea.about: The Elite Academy League is a national boys' youth platform positioned in the development pathway alongside MLS NEXT and the ECNL.
